title: Gas network craftsperson
change: Occupational standard and assessment plan revised.
overviewOfRole: Building, maintaining and repairing parts for the country's gas network, to provide a reliable supply of gas to users.

knowledges.detail: Core: The gas industry, organisations, customers and customer requirements, industry stakeholders and regulators. Health and Safety Executive.
Core: Gas network craftsperson role, responsibilities and limits of autonomy and escalation procedures. Coordination with other stakeholders and business functions, including the emergency services.
Core: Work planning and time management techniques.

Core: Awareness of health and safety regulations relevant to the craftspersons’ responsibilities: The Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations. Electricity at Work Regulations. Health and Safety at Work Act - technician's responsibilities. Managing Health and Safety at Work Regulations Provision and use of Work Equipment Regulations (PUWER). Lifting Operations and Lifting Equipment Regulations (LOLER). Dangerous Substances Explosive Atmospheres Regulations (DSEAR), ATmosphère EXplosibles (ATEX) Directives. Working at Height Regulations. Confined spaces Regulations. Control of Substances Hazardous to Health (COSHH). Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrence Regulations (RIDDOR). Noise at work regulations. Control of Asbestos regulations. Manual Handling Operations Regulations. Display Screen Equipment. Fire regulations. Building Regulations. Construction Design and Management (CDM) Regulations. Lone Working. Control of Vibration at Work Regulations.
Core: Gas emergency procedures.
Core: Emergency first aid.
The requirements and purpose of the Pressure Systems Safety Regulations (PSSR) implications of non-compliance and relevance to the role.
Core: The requirements of the Gas Safety (Management) Regulations as relevant to the role.
Core: Risk assessments, risk management techniques and approaches, method statements and control measures.
Core: Health and safety procedures and safe systems of work.
Core: Safe control of operations.

Core: Environmental and sustainability principles, regulations and guidance. Environmental hazards that can arise from gas network operations. Circular economy and re-use of materials and components. Recycling and waste management requirements. Environmental protection act and Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Directive (WEEE). Green technologies and alternative fuels.
Core: Regulatory frameworks, regulatory reporting measures and requirements.
Core: Personal protective equipment, breathing apparatus and safety equipment: what it is used for and requirements for inspection and use.
Core: Purpose, selection and use of hand tools, power tools and equipment. Pre and post use check requirements.
Core: Pre and post use check requirements and use of gas detection equipment.
Core: Storage and maintenance requirements for hand tools, power tools, gas detection equipment and other equipment.
Core: Selection and use of resources, considering materials certification, cost, quality, safety, security and environmental impact.
Core: Awareness of engineering technical specifications, standards diagrams and manufacturers' instructions relevant to role and organisation. What they are and how to use them.
Core: Standard Operating Procedures – what they are and why they are important.
Core: Safe isolation procedures for gas network assets. Reinstatement of supply.
Core: Testing and inspection procedures and the actions needed as a result of the tests.
Core: Installing, purging and commissioning gas network assets.
Core: Maintenance practices and procedures for gas network systems and assets.
Core: Problem solving, fault finding, diagnostic and rectification techniques.
Core: Asset condition and performance information and analysis techniques. Decision making and actions required.
Core: Quality assurance requirements.
Core: Change management procedures for replacing components.
Core: Documentation methods and requirements paper based and digital systems.
Core: Continuous improvement principles and techniques.
Core: Teamworking principles.
Core: Equity, diversity and inclusion in the workplace.
Core: Ethical issues and principles.
Core: Communication techniques: verbal and written.
Core: Information technology and digital systems. Awareness of General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and Cyber security.

Network Maintenance (E&I): The requirements of the current edition of the Wiring Regulations (BS7671)

Network Maintenance (Pressure management): Inspection, monitoring and testing requirements for mechanical pressure control components and equipment.
Network Maintenance (Pressure management): The requirements for corrosion inspection activities.
Network Maintenance (Pressure management): Maintenance and repair practices and techniques for mechanical equipment and components.
Network Maintenance (Pressure management): Analysis and calculation methods for mechanical system parameters. Procedures for rectification.
Network Maintenance (Pressure management): Pressure reduction principles and techniques.
Network pipelines maintenance: Mechanical theories and principles; pneumatics, hydraulics and pressure systems. Machine specifications, thermo dynamics and laminar flow theories.
Network pipelines maintenance: An awareness of the Street works code of practice requirements for the provision of signing, lighting and guarding when working in or adjacent to public highways.
Network pipelines maintenance: The pipeline safety regulations.
Network pipelines maintenance: The requirements and frequency of testing and inspection for pipelines systems and associated systems and equipment.
Network pipelines maintenance: Theories and principles of integrity testing.
Network pipelines maintenance: Non-destructive testing theories and principles.
Network pipelines maintenance: Corrosion control measures, testing procedures and their suitability.
Network pipelines maintenance: Procedures and techniques for the removal, repair and replacement of gas transportation pipelines, components and associated equipment.
Network pipelines maintenance: Maintenance policies and requirements for high pressure and low pressure storage.
Network pipelines maintenance: Valves, installation, testing, commissioning, operation and decommissioning practices and requirements.
Network pipelines maintenance: Analysis and calculation methods for pipeline system parameters. Procedures for rectification.
Network pipelines maintenance: The causes and implications of damage to pipelines and gas network assets. How to prevent damage.

Network pipelines maintenance: Principles and processes that underpin the locating of utility network assets; the requirements of health and safety guidance document 47 (HSG47) on avoiding damage to underground utility services.

behaviours.detail: Prioritises health and safety to ensure safety for self and others.
Takes responsibility for quality of work.
Supportive of the needs and concerns of others, for example relating to diversity and inclusion.
Committed to Continued Professional Development to maintain and enhance competence.
Acts ethically and upholds company values.
Collaborate within teams and with external stakeholders.

qualifications.title: Emergency First Aid at Work
qualifications.anyAdditionalInformation: This is an occupation where the type of work undertaken by craftspersons is hazardous, with a risk of harm to other staff members or the general public, the requirement for travelling and work patterns mean that employers require craftspersons to hold an emergency first aid at work qualification in order to discharge their responsibilities under the Health and Safety (First Aid) Regulations 1981. Suitable qualifications are offered by a number of Ofqual regulated awarding organisations, and the voluntary aid societies.
